title: Wake Up Dead Man, but real: how detectives find the time of death (3D)
note: pause = seconds of silence inserted BEFORE that line (the 10 s test window).

lines.text: In the movie Wake Up Dead Man, the detective solves murders by reading people.
But real detectives have a better trick. They read the body.
When you're alive, your body stays warm. Ninety-eight point six degrees.
But after a person dies, the body slowly cools down. About one and a half degrees every hour.
So if a body is six degrees colder, that person died about four hours ago.
Here's the trick. Count back from the time the temperature was taken. Not the time the body was found.
Now it's your turn. Look at the clues. Who did it?
It's B! The body is six degrees colder. That means four hours.
The temperature was taken at midnight. Four hours before midnight is eight PM. And at eight, B was out walking, all alone.
Did you count from ten, when the body was found? Then you got six PM. That's A. That's the trap!
And C found the body. Suspicious! But C was at dinner at eight.
One more thing. Hot rooms, cold rooms, clothes, and body size all change how fast a body cools.
So real detectives never say one exact time. They give a time window.
In the movie, the detective gets a confession. In real life, detectives get a window.
